title: Science: Forces & Movement 🚀
summary:
1. What is a Force?
A force is a push or a pull. We use forces every day to make things happen!

2. Changing Movement
• A force can make a stationary object (an object that is NOT moving) start to move.
• A force can speed things up, slow them down, or make a moving object stop.
• A force can also change the direction of a moving object (the way it is going).

3. Changing Shape
Forces can change the shape of an object! You can do this by:
• Stretching: Pulling things apart (like a rubber band).
• Bending: Curving an object without breaking it (like a plastic ruler).
• Folding: Bending something over itself (like paper).
• Denting: Pushing or hitting something so it gets a hollow mark (like hitting a tin can).

4. Science at Work
People use forces in their jobs! A baker pushes and pulls dough to change its shape. A footballer kicks a ball to change its direction.

questions.questionText: How does a force change the movement of a stationary toy car?
options: It makes the car start moving.
It makes the car turn into water.
questions.answer: It makes the car start moving.
questions.hint: Stationary means not moving. If you push it, what happens?

questions.questionText: If you roll a ball across the floor, how can you stop it?
options: By applying a stopping force with your hand
questions.answer: By applying a stopping force with your hand
questions.hint: You need to use your body to stop it.

questions.questionText: A tennis ball is flying towards you. You hit it back with your racket. What did the force do?
options: Changed the shape of the ball
Changed the color of the ball
Changed the direction of the ball
questions.answer: Changed the direction of the ball
questions.hint: The ball was coming AT you, now it is going AWAY from you.
